name: Plasma pen (fibroblasting)

lead: A plasma pen is a small handheld device that produces a tiny electrical arc of ionised gas between its tip and the skin. In cosmetic use it is marketed as 'fibroblasting' for tightening sagging or hooded eyelids, smoothing lines and removing small skin lesions without cutting.

It appears in looksmaxxing forums as a cheap alternative to eyelid surgery, with posts pointing to inexpensive consumer devices and much costlier clinic treatments. The sources reviewed contain no controlled trials of the cosmetic tightening claim.

paras: Proponents say the arc heats tiny points of the skin surface, producing small controlled injuries that prompt a repair response by fibroblasts and tighten the area; this explanation was not found in published studies. Scientific literature on 'plasma pens' mainly covers cold atmospheric plasma used for disinfection and wound research, which is a different application from cosmetic burning.

Because the cosmetic method works by creating small burns, no cosmetic safety trial was found, so rates of complications are unknown from the sources reviewed. A 2025 case report describes plasma pen ablation used clinically for extensive periocular xanthogranuloma.

forums.title: Plasma Pen: How to get baby-skin ,Better eye area and more

lead: A plasma pen is a handheld device that generates a small electrical arc of ionised gas, or plasma, between its tip and the skin. Marketed in cosmetics as fibroblasting or a plasma lift, it is promoted for tightening loose skin, particularly on the eyelids, and for smoothing lines and removing small blemishes.[1]

Plasma itself is described as the fourth state of matter, and non-thermal or cold atmospheric plasma has been studied for disinfection, wound care and dentistry.[2][3] Those studies concern antimicrobial and biomedical effects in the lab and clinic and are distinct from the cosmetic technique of applying hot plasma arcs to skin to tighten it.

In looksmaxxing forums the plasma pen is presented as a low-cost route to improved eyelids and skin, with users quoting device prices and comparing them with clinic fees.[1] The sources reviewed contain no controlled trials of cosmetic skin tightening with these devices.
infobox: Eyelid and skin tightening, line smoothing, lesion removal

paras: A plasma pen delivers a tiny arc between its tip and the skin surface without touching it. Proponents describe the effect as superficial tissue sublimation. Forum descriptions say the usual areas are the eyelids, nasal folds, forehead and neck.[1]

The word plasma also appears in medicine in other senses. Cold plasma devices, including a veterinary pen, have been tested against bacteria for keratitis,[4] and wound-treatment uses of cold plasma are described in reference works.[3] Wikipedia's article on cold plasma lists a 'plasma pencil' only as a device name and does not mention cosmetic tightening.[3]

The cosmetic technique intentionally causes small burns, and the sources reviewed provide no cosmetic safety dataset, so complication rates are not documented here. Studies of tissue-tolerable plasma on pig eyes examined tolerance and antiseptic efficacy for wound applications rather than for cosmetic use.[5] A 2025 case report describes plasma pen ablation used to treat extensive periocular xanthogranuloma.[6] Reference sources also note that arcing becomes possible at higher power settings with close electrode spacing.[3]

No studies found. Related research on cold plasma covers disinfection of wounds and the eye in animals and laboratory models,[4][5] a plasma-activated liquid study on cancer cell lines,[7] and the 2025 periocular xanthogranuloma case report;[6] none tests cosmetic skin tightening.

A looksmax.org thread describes the plasma pen as a way to rejuvenate sagging, wrinkled and dull skin, saying devices cost roughly $40-60 while clinic treatment ranges from $400 to $1,900, and names eyelids, nasal folds, forehead and neck as the most common treated areas.[1] A reply says the user would try it when undereyes decline.[1]

lore.intro: Looksmax.org posts present the plasma pen as an affordable alternative for eyelid and skin rejuvenation.[1]

claims.claim: A plasma pen can tighten eyelids and give 'baby-skin'.
Home plasma pens at $40-60 are an economical substitute for $400-1,900 clinic treatments.
